title: Fuel Composition Sensor — Cylinder Combustion Imbalance Bank 2
shortDescription: Flex-fuel composition sensor fault: cylinder combustion imbalance bank 2.
fullDescription: The PCM monitors the flex-fuel composition sensor to determine ethanol content of the fuel for proper injector pulse width and ignition timing. Cylinder Combustion Imbalance Bank 2 indicates a circuit or rationality fault. On flex-fuel vehicles a faulty composition sensor causes hard cold start, rough idle and reduced economy.
safetyImpact: Driveable; cold-start and economy issues likely.

causes.cause: Wiring or connector corrosion at sensor

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the flex-fuel sensor on the fuel line and inspect for corrosion or fuel residue.

fixSteps.title: Read Ethanol % on Scan Tool
fixSteps.instruction: Use bidirectional scan tool to read live ethanol percentage and frequency PID.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor Signal
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe signal pin and verify Hz signal between 50-150 Hz with key-on, engine off.

fixSteps.title: Replace Composition Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the flex-fuel composition sensor and clear codes; relearn ethanol content.

faq.q: Will it run on regular gas?
faq.a: Yes, but performance may suffer until the sensor is replaced and the PCM relearns ethanol content.

faq.q: Could bad fuel cause this?
faq.a: Yes — water or dirt in the fuel can confuse the sensor. Drain and refill with fresh fuel.

title: Cylinder 1 Injector — Contribution/Balance Bank 2 (P0271-v4)
shortDescription: Cylinder 1 fuel injector control fault (contribution/balance bank 2). Stored as P0271-v4.
fullDescription: The PCM detects a fault in the cylinder 1 injector control circuit or its driver. Contribution/Balance Bank 2 can be triggered by a stuck-open injector, an open coil, a wiring fault, or a failed PCM driver. Continued driving with a faulty injector can hydro-lock the engine or wash down the cylinder bore.
safetyImpact: Drive with caution; raw fuel can damage catalyst and dilute oil.

causes.cause: Wiring chafe or connector fault at injector
Low fuel pressure causing injector misfire

fixSteps.title: Swap Injector to Adjacent Cylinder
fixSteps.instruction: Move the injector to a known-good cylinder and see if the misfire follows.

fixSteps.title: Measure Injector Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect injector connector and measure across terminals; compare to spec (typically 12-16 Ω).

fixSteps.title: Check Driver Signal
fixSteps.instruction: Use noid light or scope to confirm PCM is pulsing the injector.

fixSteps.title: Replace Injector or Repair Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the injector or repair the wiring/connector and re-test.

faq.q: Can I drive with a bad injector?
faq.a: Briefly, but a stuck-open injector can wash the cylinder and dilute oil. Fix promptly.

faq.q: Should I replace all injectors?
faq.a: Not always — but on high-mileage engines a full set is often economical labor-wise.

title: Turbo/Supercharger Bypass Valve — Bypass Valve A Stuck Closed (P02D0-v3)
shortDescription: Turbocharger bypass / blow-off valve fault: bypass valve a stuck closed. Stored as P02D0-v3.
fullDescription: The PCM monitors the turbocharger bypass (recirculation) valve for proper response. Bypass Valve A Stuck Closed indicates a circuit fault or a stuck valve that fails to bleed boost between throttle lifts. A stuck valve causes compressor surge, broken inlet hoses, and torque limp.
safetyImpact: Driveable; risk of compressor damage and inlet hose failure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Valve & Vacuum Lines
fixSteps.instruction: Visually inspect the bypass valve, vacuum hoses, and inlet boot for cracks or disconnects.

fixSteps.title: Command Valve via Scan Tool
fixSteps.instruction: Use bidirectional scan tool to actuate the bypass solenoid and listen for click.

fixSteps.title: Test Solenoid Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure solenoid resistance and compare to specification.

fixSteps.title: Replace Bypass Valve
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the bypass / blow-off valve assembly and re-clear codes.

faq.q: Is compressor surge harmful?
faq.a: Yes — repeated surge can damage the compressor wheel and shaft seals.

faq.q: Can I drive with this code?
faq.a: Yes briefly, but high-boost driving should be avoided until the valve is fixed.
